claims.text: RFC 9457 defines the Problem Details JSON object with members type, title, status, and detail (plus instance, not covered here) as the standard shape for an HTTP API error response.
claims.source_hint: RFC 9457, section 3 ("The Problem Details JSON Object")

claims.text: RFC 9457: the type member is optional; when it is not present, its value is assumed to be "about:blank", meaning the problem has no more specific semantics than the HTTP status code alone.
RFC 9457: the status member is the HTTP status code generated by the origin server, meant to be the same code already on the response's status line, repeated for convenience.

The Caddyfile's @missingOrder handler responds to a missing order with status 404, header Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8, and body {"error":"order not found"} — one ad-hoc field, no standard shape.

The Caddyfile's /conflict handler responds with status 409 and the plain-text body "Conflict: this order was already paid", with no Content-Type header set (Caddy's respond directive defaults to text/plain for a plain string).
RFC 9457 applies to HTTP API error responses in general, not only 5xx server errors; its examples and abstract cover client-error statuses like 403 and 503 alike.

Live this session: GET /conflict on the running lab (localhost:8080) returns HTTP 409, Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8, Content-Length: 37, and the exact body "Conflict: this order was already paid" — no JSON, no error field.
